saints.name: St. James
saints.title: Apostle
saints.shortBlurb: Son of Zebedee, brother of John, one of the three closest to the Lord and the first Apostle to die for the faith…
biography: James the Greater, son of Zebedee and Salome and elder brother of John, fished the Sea of Galilee in partnership with Peter when the Lord called the brothers from their nets. With Peter and John he alone witnessed the raising of Jairus's daughter, the Transfiguration, and the agony in Gethsemane.

Jesus named the brothers Boanerges, 'sons of thunder'; when their mother asked the chief seats, he promised them his cup of suffering. He drank it first of the Twelve: at the Passover of 44, Herod Agrippa I 'killed James, the brother of John, with the sword' (Acts 12:2) — the only apostolic martyrdom recorded in Scripture.

Clement of Alexandria relates that the man who had accused James, moved by his confession, declared himself a Christian and was beheaded with him. A later tradition carried his relics to Compostela in Spain, where from the ninth century his shrine became, with Rome and Jerusalem, the third great pilgrimage of Christendom.

He is patron of Spain, whose sons called on Santiago in battle; of pilgrims, who still bear his scallop shell along the roads of Europe to his tomb; and of laborers, as the fisherman who left his nets at Christ's word.
saints.knownFor: The first Apostle martyred; patron of pilgrims to Compostela.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 25 July
